questions.question: Which of the following is the best practice for creating a strong and secure password?
options: Using your birth date and city
Using '12345678' for all accounts
Using a mix of uppercase, lowercase, numbers, and symbols
Using your pet's name
questions.hint: Think about making the password complex and hard for others to guess.

questions.question: If you receive an unexpected email from your bank asking you to click a link and enter your password to 'verify your account', what should you do?
options: Click the link and update your password immediately
Reply to the email asking if it is real
Delete the email or report it as phishing
Forward the email to all your friends to warn them
questions.hint: Legitimate companies rarely ask for passwords via email links.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of Two-Factor Authentication (2FA)?
options: To allow you to log in without a password
To provide an extra layer of security beyond just a password
To encrypt your hard drive automatically
To speed up the login process
questions.hint: It requires two different forms of identification to grant access.

questions.question: Under the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), what does the 'Right to Erasure' (Right to be Forgotten) allow individuals to do?
options: Change their legal name on all platforms
Request that a company delete their personal data
Hide their profile from search engines only
Access all the company's internal documents
questions.hint: Focus on the word 'Erasure' and how it relates to your personal information.

questions.question: When using a public Wi-Fi network at a cafe, which tool is most effective for protecting your data from being intercepted by others on the same network?
options: A standard Antivirus software
A Virtual Private Network (VPN)
An Ad-blocker browser extension
A Password Manager
questions.hint: Look for a tool that creates a secure, encrypted tunnel for your internet traffic.
